content: 1. A utility sink in a food service area is defined as any sink that is not intended for handwashing or warewashing purposes. 2. A wading pool is a recreational water facility with a maximum depth of less than 1 meter and is not designed for use by children. 3. Passageways must be sized to prevent the storage of bulk food items unless the passageways are specifically designed to meet provision room standards. 4. Refrigeration and hot-food holding facilities, including temporary storage units, must be available in all food preparation and service areas, as well as for food being transported to remote areas. 5. Food flow within a vessel must be arranged in a logical sequence to eliminate or minimize cross-traffic or backtracking. 6. There must be a clear separation between clean and soiled operations in food service areas. 7. When a common corridor is used for both clean and soiled operations, the minimum distance from bulkhead to bulkhead must be considered. 8. Within a galley, the standard separation between clean and soiled operations must be at least 2 meters (6½ feet). For smaller galleys, the minimum distance will be assessed during the plan review. 9. 10. Food must flow in an orderly manner from suppliers at dockside through food storage, preparation, and finishing areas to service areas, and finally to waste management areas. 11. A size profile must be provided for each food area, including provisions, preparation rooms, galleys, pantries, warewash areas, garbage processing areas, and storage spaces. The size profile must indicate the square meters of space designated for each area. 12. The Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) may visit profile vessels to verify capacity during operational inspections. 13. The size profile must be an established standard for each cruise line, based on the line's review of area sizes for similar food areas in its existing vessels. 14. As ship size and passenger/crew totals change, there must be a proportional adjustment in the size of each food area to meet service needs. 15. Size evaluations of food areas will incorporate seating capacity, staffing, service, and equipment requirements. 16. During the plan review process, the VSP evaluates the size of specific rooms or areas and the flow of food through the vessel to those areas. 17. The VSP will also use operational inspection results to review size profiles submitted by individual cruise lines. 18. Equipment in galleys must meet the requirements outlined in sections 6.2.1.1 through 6.2.1.12, depending on the level and type of service, and may also be recommended for other areas. 19. Blast chillers must be incorporated into the design of passenger and crew galleys. More than one unit may be necessary depending on the vessel's size and the distances between the blast chillers and storage/service areas. 20. The size and type of blast chillers installed in each food preparation area must align with the menu concept, operational requirements, and the volume of food requiring cooling. 21. Food preparation utility sinks must be included in all meat, fish, and vegetable preparation rooms, cold pantries, garde mangers, and any other areas where personnel wash or soak food. Automatic vegetable washing machines may be used in addition to utility sinks in vegetable preparation rooms. 22. Storage cabinets, shelves, or racks for food products and equipment must be included in food storage, preparation, and service areas, including bars and pantries. 23. Fixed or portable tables, carts, or pallets must be located in areas where food or ice is dispensed from cooking equipment, such as soup kettles, steamers, braising pans, tilting pans, or ice storage bins. 24. Storage cabinets or racks for large utensils, such as ladles, paddles, whisks, and spatulas, must be provided, along with vertical storage for cutting boards. 25. Deck drains, scuppers, and sinks must be sized to eliminate spillage and overflow onto adjacent deck surfaces. 26. Sufficient deck drainage must be provided, and deck and scupper drain lines in food service and warewash areas must be designed to prevent liquids from pooling on the decks. 27. Deck sinks must not be used as substitutes for deck drains. 28. Cross-drain connections must be provided to prevent pooling and spillage from scuppers when the vessel is listing. 29. If nonremovable coaming is provided around deck drains, the juncture with the deck must be coved. Integral coving is not required. 30. Ramps installed over thresholds must be easily removable or sealed in place, sloped for easy trolley roll-in and roll-out, and strong enough to maintain their shape. If ramps over scupper covers are part of the scupper system, they must be constructed of smooth, durable, and easily cleanable materials. 31. The installation of drain lines carrying black water or other liquid wastes must be limited in spaces used for food preparation or storage, including areas for washing or storing utensils and equipment (e.g., bars, deck pantries, and over buffet counters). If unavoidable, steel piping must be sleeve-welded or butt-welded, and plastic piping must be heat-fused or chemically welded. 32. Factory-assembled transition fittings for steel-to-plastic pipes are allowed for scupper lines when manufactured per ASTM F1973 or equivalent standards. Push-fit or press-fit piping must not be used in these areas. 33. Handwashing sinks in food areas must be supplied with hot and cold potable water at a temperature between 38°C (100°F) and 49°C (120°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. 34. Handwashing sinks in food areas must be constructed of stainless steel. In food service areas and bars, sinks may be constructed of a similar, smooth, durable material. 35. Handwashing stations must include a soap dispenser, paper towel dispenser, corrosion-resistant waste receptacle, and, where necessary, splash panels to protect adjoining equipment, clean utensils, food storage, or food preparation surfaces. 36. If soap dispensers, paper towel dispensers, and waste receptacles are attached to the bulkhead, they must be permanently sealed or made removable for cleaning. Air hand dryers are not permitted. 37. Soap and paper towel dispensers must not be installed over adjoining equipment, clean utensil storage, food storage, food preparation surfaces, bar counters, or water fountains. 38. For multiple-station sinks, a soap dispenser must be within 380 millimeters (15 inches) of each faucet, and a paper towel dispenser must be within 760 millimeters (30 inches) of each faucet. 39.
